task.title: Keep the board's poll tag still while assignment wording ages
task.description:
The board's poll became conditional in "Stop the board resending the whole task list every second": `serveTasks` (internal/webui/handler.go) tags the encoded document with a sha256 ETag and answers a matching `If-None-Match` with `304 Not Modified`, so an idle board costs headers only. One input to that document still changes on its own clock: the assignment chip's wording. `taskPresentation` calls `time.Now()` and `presentation.AssignedAgo` (internal/presentation/board.go) renders "assigned just now", then "assigned N minutes ago", hours, days. Each time that phrase crosses a boundary the document's bytes change, the tag moves, and every open board downloads, parses and redraws the whole document (437 KB on this repo) even though no task changed.

Measured by the branch's final review: a task assigned 59.5 s earlier, read, then read again one second later with the first tag, answered 200 with a new tag. A board with five assignments under an hour old re-reads about five full documents a minute instead of none. This repo has no assignments today, so it does not show here; an agent-heavy board (many short-lived claims) is exactly where it does.

Correctness is unaffected: this is the remaining idle cost, not a bug.

## Possible approaches

- Send the assignment's `createdAt` (already in the task) and let the page derive the wording, re-deriving it on its own timer. The presentation rule then lives in two places, which is what the server-side composition was meant to avoid (see the comment above `followOpenThreadPanels` in internal/webui/assets/index.html); a shared, tested rule table or a server-sent rule would be needed.
- Keep the wording on the server but leave it out of the polled document: serve it from a separate, cheaper read, or have the document carry the next boundary time so the page knows when to ask again.
- Exclude the time-derived fields from the hash while still sending them. Rejected unless proven safe: a 304 would then leave stale wording on screen indefinitely.

## Acceptance

- An idle board with fresh assignments receives 304 on every poll while no task, vocabulary or identity changes.
- The assignment chip's wording still advances (just now, minutes, hours, days) on an open board without a reload.
- Go handler test: the tag does not change across an "assigned N ago" boundary when nothing else changed.
- Page test: the chip's wording advances while polls answer 304.
